### Result

\nX-twitter\nIMPORTANT COURT AND WEATHER ALERTS\nAO 2025-001\nDownload the PDF\nIN THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT OF FLORIDA\nADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO.\nAO 2025-001\nIN RE:CIVIL CASE MANAGEMENT\n\nIN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT,\nIN AND FOR COLUMBIA, DIXIE, HAMILTON, LAFAYETTE, MADISON, SUWANNEE AND TAYLOR COUNTIES, FLORIDA\n\nADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO, 2025-001\n(Supersedes AO2021-004 and AO2021-005B)\n\nINRE: CIVIL CASE MANAGEMENT\n\nWHEREAS, on May 23, 2024, the Florida Supreme Court issued Administrative Order SC2023-09621 (1), amending the Florida Rules of Civil Procedure and requiring the chief judge of each judicial circuit to enter an administrative order addressing certain case management\nrequirements, including the issuance of case management orders, deadlines for completing certain pretrial matters, and setting trial dates consistent with the time standards specified in the\nFlorida Rules of General Practice and Judicial Administration.\n\nWHEREAS, each civil case must be assigned within 120 days after the action commences to a complex, general, or streamlined case management track.\n\nWHEREAS, Rule 1.200 (i) requires that form case management orders will be set by the chief judge of\neach circuit for general and streamlined cases.\n\nWHEREAS, Florida Rules of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.545(a), (b), and (e),\nrespectively, require judges to conclude litigation as soon as it is reasonably and justly\npossible to do so, to take charge of all cases at an early stage and to control the progress of the\ncase thereafter until it is determined, and to apply a firm continuance policy allowing\ncontinuances only for good cause shown.\n\nNOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me as the Chief Judge of the Third Judicial\nCircuit, specifically, Article V, section 2(d) of the Florida Constitution, sections 40.001 and\n43.26, Florida Statutes, and Florida Rule of Judicial Administration 2.215, it is\ntherefore ORDERED as follows:\n\n1 On December 5, 2024, the Florida Supreme Court issued an amended order and mle\nlanguage after receiving comments and conducting oral arguments regarding the amendments\nannounced in its May 23, 2024, opinion. See In Re: Amendments to Florida Rules of Civil Procedure, No. SC2023-0962, 2024 WL 4983566 (Fla. Dec. 5, 2024), op’n corrected January 23, 2025. This Administrative Order incorporates the amended requirements.\n\nA.O. 2025-001 (In Re: CM/ Case Management)\n\nI. TERMS AND DEFINITIONS\n\nA. “Civil Cases” – Under rule 1.200, civil cases2 are differentiated as follows:\n\n1. “Complex” cases are actions designated by court order as complex under rule\n1.201(a). Complex cases must proceed as provided in rule 1.201.\n\n2. “General” cases are all other actions that do not meet the criteria for streamlined or\ncomplex.\n\n3. “Streamlined” cases are actions that reflect some mutual knowledge about the\nunderlying facts, have limited needs for discovery, well-established legal issues related\nto liability and damages, few anticipated dispositive pretrial motions, minimal documentary\nevidence, and an anticipated trial length of no more than 3 days. Uncontested circuit cases and\nall county civil cases should generally be presumed to be streamlined cases.\n\nB. “Commencement” – Pursuant to rule 1.050, every action of a civil nature shall be deemed\ncommenced when the complaint or petition is filed except that ancillary proceedings\nshall be deemed commenced when the writ is issued or the pleading setting forth the claim of the\nparty initiating the action is filed.\n\nII. CASE MANAGEMENT – GENERAL REQUIREMENTS\n\nA. In contested cases subject to this order, the parties are required to diligently participate in\ncase management, including engaging in early consultation and cooperation, early\ninteraction with a Civil Case Manager and early involvement with the Court. Parties are also\nrequired to adhere to case-specific compliance deadlines as established in case\nmanagement orders, confer in a good faith attempt to narrow or resolve matters in\ncontroversy, and identify issues that require direct involvement by the Court. If a case\nmanagement conference is scheduled, attendance by trial counsel and those parties who are not\nrepresented by counsel is mandatory.\n\nB. Failure to appear at a case management or pretrial conference or failure to comply with the\nterms of this order may result in such sanctions as are just and lawful including: an immediate ex\nparte hearing and entry of final judgment or default or dismissal, limitation of witnesses or\nother evidence, striking of claims or defenses, or imposition of attorney fees or costs.\n\n \n\n2 Rule 1.200 exempts many different types of civil actions from the rule’s general requirements.\nSee R. 1.200 (a). Some examples of exempted actions include: certain actions under the\nFlorida Small Claims Rules; petitions for habeas corpus or other extraordinary writs; actions\nto enforce or quash an administrative summons or subpoena; and, eminent domain actions under\narticle X, section 6 of the Florida Constitution or chapters 73 and 74, Florida Statutes.\n2\n\nA.O. 1025-001 (In Re: Civil Case Management)\n\nC. Parties must mediate by the Court’s deadline. The parties are responsible for assuring that\nthey have all the necessary information to value their position prior to mediation. If the\nparties fail to mediate without good cause before the mediation deadline, sanctions shall\nbe imposed by the Court. Failure to timely mediate shall not constitute just cause for a trial\ncontinuance.\n\nD. Extensions of deadlines established in case management orders are governed by rule\n1.200 or rule 1.201, and trial continuances are governed by rule 1.460.\n\nIII. CASE MANAGEMENT ORDERS – STREAMLINED AND GENERAL CASES\n\nA. Within 120 days after the commencement of any civil case subject to rule 1.200, the presiding\njudge in the case must review and designate the case as “Complex,” “Streamlined,” or “General” and issue a case management order for each streamlined or general civil case, complete with the applicable deadlines. Standardized orders for streamlined cases (Appendix A) and general cases (Appendix B) are attached hereto.\n\nB. A change in case designation may be made by the presiding judge on the judge’s own initiative\nor upon motion of any party. Should any party assert that a civil case should be treated other\nthan designated above, such party shall file a written motion requesting such change and the motion shall be expeditiously resolved by the presiding judge.\n\nC. Case management orders must specify, at a minimum, deadlines for the following case events:\n\n1. Service of complaints;\n2. Service under extensions;\n3. Adding new parties;\n4. Completion of fact discovery;\n5. Completion of expert discovery;\n6. Filing and service of motions for summary judgment:\n7. Resolution of all objections to pleadings;\n8. Resolution of all pretrial motions;\n9. Completion of alternative dispute resolution; and,\n10. Projected trial date. [Actual trial date(s) shall be set by subsequent order.]\n\nD. Deadlines must be consistent with the time standards specified in Florida Rule of General\nPractice and Judicial Administration 2.250 (a)(l)(B).\n\nE. Plaintiff (if self-represented) or Plaintiff’s counsel must file a Notice of Final Service\n\n3\n\nA.O. 21125-001 (In Re: Civil Case Management)\n\n(“notice”) when the last-named defendant has been served with the complaint. The notice must be\nfiled within five days of final service. Failure to file and serve the notice as required by this\nparagraph may result in the imposition of sanctions.\n\nF. If any party desires to amend the initial case management order, an amended case\nmanagement order meeting the time and form requirements set forth in this Order may be prepared and stipulated to by the parties. The agreed order may extend a deadline if the extension does not affect the ability to comply with the remaining dates in the case management\norder. The proposed order should be submitted for final approval by the presiding judge.\nParties’ requests for trial continuances are governed by rule 1.460 and if a trial is not reached\nduring the trial period set by court order, the court must enter an order setting a new trial\nperiod that is as soon as practicable, given the needs of the case and resources of the court.\n\nG. Rule 1.200 as amended is intended to supersede any case management rules issued by circuit\ncourts and administrative orders on case management to the extent of contradiction.3 Neither this Administrative Order nor the attached model orders shall be construed as granting any\nrights not already provided for by rule, statute, or law. Case management orders already in\neffect on January 1, 2025, continue to govern pending actions; however, any extensions of\ndeadlines specified in those existing case management orders are governed by amended rule\n1.200 or amended rule 1.201. For actions commenced before January 1, 2025, and in which the court has not issued a case management order by that date, a case management order must be issued by April 4, 2025.\n\nIV. CONFERENCES\n\nA. Case Management Conferences\n\n1. Conferences may be set by the court or by a party upon reasonable notice. Notices by parties\nmust identify specific issues to be addressed and contain a list of all pending motions.\n2. Motions for summary judgment and motions requiring evidentiary hearings may not be heard as part of a case management conference, unless agreed to by the parties.\n3. Attorneys and self-represented litigants appearing at conferences must be prepared on the\npending matters in the case, be prepared to make decisions about future progress of the case and\nhave authority to make representations to the court and enter into binding agreements\nconcerning motions, issues and scheduling.\n4. Failure to appear may result in sanctions including dismissal of the action, striking of\npleadings, limiting proof or witnesses, or any other appropriate action by the Court.\n\n3 See In Re: Amendments to Florida Rules of Civil Procedure, No. SC2023-0962, 2024 WL 4983566 at\n*8 (Fla. Dec. 5, 2024), op’n corrected January 23, 2025 (Court Commentary, 2024 Amendment).\n4\n\nA.O. 2025-00/ (In Re: Civil Case Management)\n\nB. Pretrial Conferences\n\n1. Once the case has been set for an actual trial period, the Court or a party may set a\nconference to consider and determine the issues to be tried, stipulations, witnesses and evidence,\nlogistics and scheduling, jury instructions and verdict forms, or any other appropriate trial\nplanning matters.\n\nV. DISCOVERY\n\nA party must, without awaiting a discovery request, provide to the other parties certain\ninitial discovery disclosures unless privileged or protected from disclosure. Seer. 1.280(a),\nFla.R.Civ.P4. A party may not seek discovery from any source before that party’s initial\ndisclosure obligations are satisfied, except when authorized by stipulation or by court order. The\ndiscovery rules are to be construed and applied in accordance with the federal\nproportionality standard. Grounds for objection must be provided with specificity,\nincluding the reasons. Objections must state whether any responsive materials are being withheld\non the basis of that objection. An objection to part of a request must specify the part and\npermit inspection of the rest. Written discovery shall be propounded promptly. Any use of\nstandard interrogatories must be adjusted for proportional discovery.\n\nVI. CASE MANAGEMENT – COMPLEX CASES\n\nRule 1.200 as amended does not require the Chief Judge to set the form for case\nmanagement orders in complex cases. Complex litigation is governed by Rule 1.201, and the Court\nmay hold a hearing to determine whether any case should be designated as complex.\nCounsel for the parties and pro se individuals representing themselves in complex cases\nmay believe that the unique circumstances presented in their cases support the entry of a case\nmanagement order tailored to the cause and agreed to by the litigants rather than an order\nunilaterally issued by the presiding judge. Therefore, the parties are encouraged to consult\nand confer in an effort to draft a mutually acceptable Agreed Mandatory Civil Case\nManagement Order for submission to the court that addresses mandatory deadlines and moves\nthe case to disposition in a timely fashion. This should be done as soon as reasonably possible\nbecause a case management order must issue within ten (10) days after completion of an initial\ncase management conference. A final case management conference must be scheduled not less than\n90 days before the date the case is set for trial. In complex cases, parties must notify\nthe court immediately if a case management conference or hearing time becomes\nunnecessary. Motions for trial\n\n4 Parties are cautioned to review Fla. R. Civ. P. 1.280 in its entirety and to familiarize\nthemselves with the 2024 amendments to the rnle.\n5\n\nA.O. 2025-00/ (In Re: Civil Case Management)\n\ncontinuances in complex cases are governed by rule 1.460.\n\nVII. CONCLUSION\n\nCounsel for the parties and prose individuals who are representing themselves in pending civil\ncases, whether in circuit court or county court civil divisions, shall review the Supreme Court\ncase management and resolution provisions contained in AOSC2023-0962, as well as Fla. R. Jud. Admin 2.250 and 2.545. Thereafter, they shall review their pending civil cases with the\nrequirements of the Supreme Court and this local administrative order in mind.\n\nDONE AND ORDERED in Chambers in Lake City, Columbia County, Florida, this 26th day of February, 2025.\n\n6\n\nA.O. 2025-001 (APPENDIX A)\n\nIN THE [COUNTY or CIRCUIT] COURT IN AND FOR [COUNTY] COUNTY, FLORIDA\n\n[PLAINTIFF(S)]\nPlaintiff(s),\n\nCase Number: (CASE NO.)\nDivision: (DIVISION)\n\nv.\n\n[DEFENDANT(S)]\nDefendant(s).\n\nCIVIL CASE MANAGEMENT ORDER – STREAMLINED CASES\n\nPursuant to Florida Rule of Civil Procedure 1.200, the Court finds this case should be assigned to\na streamlined case management track. Pursuant to Florida Rule of General Practice and\nJudicial Administration 2.250(a)(l )(8), the expected completion date of a nonjury case is 12\nmonths from the date of service of initial process on the last defendant or 120 days after\ncommencement of the action as provided in rule 1.050, whichever occurs first.\n\nThe initial complaint was filed on [DATm. Accordingly, the following terms and deadlines shall\napply in this case:\n\nI. CASE DEADLINES AND EVENTS\n\nA. Deadline for service of complaints: 120 days after the complaint is filed.\nB. Deadline for service under extensions: 150 days after the complaint is filed.\nC. Deadline for addition of new parties: 180 days after the complaint is filed.\nD. Deadline for completion of fact discovery: 240 days after the complaint is filed.\nE. Deadline for completion of expert discovery: 270 days after the complaint is filed.\nF. Deadline for filing and service of motions for summary judgment: 90 days before\ntrial. Motions for summary judgment must comply with rule l.510(b) and be resolved no later than 15\ndays before trial.\nG. Motion hearings: within 20 days of filing any motion for which a hearing is required, the\nmoving party must contact the presiding judges office to set the motion for hearing.\nH. Deadline for all objections to pleadings to be resolved: within 60 days after the objection is\nfiled and no later than 30 days before the pretrial conference.\nI. Deadline for all pretrial motions to be resolved (excluding motions for summary judgment):\nwithin 30 days after the motion is filed and no later than the Friday before the trial week.\nJ. Deadline for completion of alternative dispute resolution including mediation: 270 days after\nthe complaint is filed.\n\n1\n\nA.O. 2025-001 (APPENDIX A)\n\nK. Projected trial date: 12 months after the complaint is filed. Not later than 45 days before\nthe projected trial period, a firm trial date will be determined and ordered by the presiding judge\nif the firm trial date has not otherwise already been set pursuant to Florida Rule of\nCivil Procedure 1.400(c).\n\nII. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\nA. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) provides parties with an out-of-court alternative to\nsettling disagreements through mediation. All parties must mediate prior to trial unless\nexcused by court order for good cause shown or as otherwise required by law and in\ncompliance with the Rules of Civil Procedure.\nB. Notices of unavailability have no effect on the deadlines set by the case management order. If\na party is unable to comply with a deadline in a case management order, the party must take action consistent with rule 1.200. The Court will consider a request to approve changes to these\ndeadlines upon a showing of good cause by either party based on matters arising from an\nemergency or unavailability. Procrastination in completing discovery or mediation will not\nconstitute good cause for a change to these deadlines.\nC. Motions to continue trial are disfavored and should rarely be granted and then only upon\ngood cause shown. Any motion to continue a trial date must comply with rule 1.460.\nD. In cases wherein one party is unrepresented (prose), it is the responsibility for the sole\nattorney in the case to serve within five business days this Order upon any pro se party who does\nnot have access to and is not a registered user of the Florida Courts e-Filing Portal.\n\nIT IS ORDERED that all parties shall abide by the terms of this Order. Deadlines will be strictly\nenforced unless changed by court order. Failure by a party to follow the deadlines in this Order\nmay result in the imposition of sanctions.\n\nDONE AND ORDERED in _______________COUNTY, FLORIDA.\n\n(COUNTY or CIRCUIT JUDGE)\nJUDGE\n\n \n\nCopies:\n\n2\n\nA.O. 2025-001 (APPENDIX B)\n\n \n\nIN THE [COUNTY or CIRCUIT] COURT IN AND FOR (COUNTY) COUNTY, FLORIDA\n\n \n\n[PLAINTIFF(S)]\n\nPlaintiff(s),\n\n \n\nCase Number: [CASE NO.]\nDivision: [DIVISION]\n\n \n\nv.\n\n[DEFENDANT(S)]\nDefendant(s).\n——————-‘/\n\nCIVIL CASE MANAGEMENT ORDER- GENERAL CASES\nPursuant to Florida Rule of Civil Procedure 1.200, the Court finds this case should be assigned to\na general case management track. Pursuant to Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial\nAdministration 2.250(a)(l)(B), the expected completion date of a jury case is 18 months from the\ndate of service of initial process on the last defendant or 120 days after commencement of the\naction as provided in rule 1.050, whichever occurs first.\n\nThe initial complaint was filed on (DATE). Accordingly, the following terms and deadlines shall\napply in this case:\n\nI. CASE DEADLINES AND EVENTS\n\nA. Deadline for service of complaints: 120 days after the complaint is filed.\nB. Deadline for service under extensions: 180 days after the complaint is filed.\nC. Deadline for addition of new parties: 210 days after the complaint is filed.\nD. Deadline for completion of fact discovery: 420 days after the complaint is filed.\nE. Deadline for completion of expert discovery: 450 days after the complaint is filed.\nF. Deadline for filing and service of motions for summary judgment: 120 days before trial. Motions for summary judgment must comply with rule 1.51O(b) and be resolved no later than 30 days before trial.\nG. Motion hearings: within 20 days of filing any motion for which a hearing is required, the\nmoving party must contact the presiding judges office to set the motion for hearing.\nH. Deadline for all objections to pleadings to be resolved: within 75 days after the objection is\nfiled and no later than 45 days before the pretrial conference.\nI. Deadline for all pretrial motions to be resolved (excluding motions for summary\njudgment): within 60 days after the motion is filed and no later than the Friday before the trial\nweek.\nJ. Projected trial date: 18 months after the complaint is filed. Not later than 45 days before\nthe projected trial period, a firm trial date will be determined and ordered by the presiding judge\nif the firm trial date has not otherwise already been set pursuant to Florida Rule of\nCivil Procedure 1.400(c).\n\nII. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\nA. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) provides parties with an out-of-court alternative to\nsettling disagreements through mediation. All parties must mediate prior to trial unless excused\nby court order for good cause shown or as otherwise required by law and in compliance\nwith the Rules of Civil Procedure.\nB. Notices of unavailability have no effect on the deadlines set by the case management order. If\na party is unable to comply with a deadline in a case management order, the party must take action consistent with rule 1.200. The Court will consider a request to approve changes to these\ndeadlines upon a showing of good cause by either party based on matters arising from an emergency or unavailability. Procrastination in completing discovery or mediation will not constitute good cause for a change to these deadlines.\nC. Motions to continue trial are disfavored and should rarely be granted and then only upon good\ncause shown. Any motion to continue a trial date must comply with rule 1.460.\nD. In cases wherein one party is unrepresented (“pro se”), it is the responsibility for the\nsole attorney in the case to serve within five business days this Order upon any pro se party who\ndoes not have access to and is not a registered user of the Florida Courts e-Filing Portal.\n\nIT IS ORDERED that all parties shall abide by the tenns of this Order. Deadlines will be strictly\nenforced unless changed by court order. Failure by a party to follow the deadlines in this Order\nmay result in the imposition of sanctions.\n\nDONE AND ORDERED in ______ COUNTY, FLORIDA.\n\n[COUNTY or CIRCUIT JUDGE]\nJUDGE\n\nCopies:\n2\n\nMelissa Olin, Chief Judge\nBack To Orders\n\n\n\n\n\nPress Escape to close the search panel.\nX Feed | Circuit3FL\n\nJudge Kathryn R. to content\nSkip to content\nHOME\nJUDGES\nCOUNTIES\nORDERS\nSERVICES\nCOURT CALENDAR\nCIVIL CASE MANAGEMENT\nADA\nAttorneys\nDirectory\nFamily Forms\nFAQ\nJurors\nMedia\nResources\nSelf Help\nFacebook-f\n \nX-twitter\nIMPORTANT COURT AND WEATHER ALERTS\nAO 2025-005\nDownload the PDF\nIN THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT OF FLORIDA\nADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO.\n2025-005\nIN RE:ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER ESTABLISHING COURT FACILITY SECURITY PROCEDURES WITHIN THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT (SUPERSEDES AO 2018-022)\n\nIN THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT OF FLORIDA\nADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO.: 2025-005\n(Supersedes Administrative Order No.: 2018-022)\nADMINISTRATIVE ORDER ESTABLISHING COURT FACILITY SECURITY\nPROCEDURES WITHIN THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT\nWHEREAS, pursuant to Article V, Section 2(d) of the Florida Constitution, the Chief Judge is\nresponsible for the administrative supervision of the courts in their circuit;\nWHEREAS, pursuant to Rule 2.215, Florida Rules of General Practice and Judicial\nAdministration, and Section 43 .26, Florida Statutes, along with the inherent power of the Court\nto do all things reasonable and necessary for the administration of justice, the Court finds that it\nis necessary and reasonable to enact this policy;\nWHEREAS, on September 25, 2025, the Florida Supreme Court, via memorandum, affirmed\nthat chief judges continue to have the authority to prohibit weapons (including firearms) in\ncourthouses and courtrooms and that the exercise of that authority is consistent with the public\npolicy embodied in Florida’s gun laws and is grounded in the power granted to chief judges by\narticle V, section 2 of the Florida Constitution, by the Florida Statutes, and by the Rules of\nGeneral Practice and Judicial Administration;\nWHEREAS, pursuant to Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration\n2.215(b )(7), the Chief Judge “must regulate the use of all court facilities” and the Chief Judge\nrecognizes that the security of court facilities is a daily concern due in part to the emotional\nnature of many court proceedings. Further, the Chief Judge recognizes the need to ensure the\nhealth, safety, and welfare of those who work within the court facilities or who litigate or\notherwise conduct business within the facilities and to ensure that justice is administered without\nthe potential for intimidation. Moreover, the Chief Judge recognizes the need to protect the\npublic interest in providing for orderly and safe passage for the transaction of court business\nthroughout the various court facilities;\nWHEREAS, a court has the inherent authority to designate its own facilities, including the\nreasonably necessary boundaries thereof and entry points to ensure an appropriate level of\nsecurity and to ensure the efficient operation of judicial proceedings and court business;\nWHEREAS, pursuant to section 26.49, Florida Statutes, the Sheriffs of the Circuit are the\nExecutive Officers of the circuit court, required by section 30.15(l)(c), Florida Statutes, in\nperson or by deputy to attend all terms of the circuit and county courts held within their\nrespective counties;\nWHEREAS, section 790.06 (12), Florida Statutes, states that a license to carry a concealed\nweapon or firearm does not authorize any person to openly carry a handgun or carry a concealed\nweapon or concealed firearm into a courthouse or courtroom, but that a judge is not precluded\nfrom carrying a concealed weapon or firearm or from determining who will carry a concealed\nweapon or concealed firearm in his or her courtroom;\nAO 2025-005 (Court Facility Security Procedures Within the Third Judicial Circuit)\nWHEREAS, it is necessary and proper to regulate the possession of firearms, weapons, and\nother destructive devices, as well as chemicals and other explosive materials, within court\nfacilities in the Third Judicial Circuit to protect members of the public, jurors, judges, other court\nofficers, and staff to ensure a secure environment for the orderly and safe administration of\njustice.\nIT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:\nI. “COURT FACILITIES” DEFINED:\nPursuant to section 29.008(1)(a), Florida Statutes:\n“Facility” means reasonable and necessary buildings and office space and\nappurtenant equipment and furnishings, structures, real estate, easements, and\nrelated interests in real estate, including, but not limited to, those for the\npurpose of housing legal materials for use by the general public and personnel,\nequipment, or functions of the circuit or county courts, public defenders’\noffices, state attorneys’ offices, and court-related functions of the office of the\nclerks of the circuit and county courts and all storage. [ … ] The term also\nincludes access to parking1 for such facilities in connection with such courtrelated\nfunctions that may be available free or from a private provider or a\nlocal government for a fee.\nCourt facilities are facilities in which the court conducts its official business including the areas\ninside and around the premises of a courthouse, courthouse annex, judicial center, justice center,\nhistoric courthouse, or other building where court functions are performed by the court or on\nbehalf of the court for the furtherance of court operations and cases. The Chief Judge determines\nthat pursuant to section 29.008(1)(a), “court facilities” in the Third Judicial Circuit are the following:\nA. Columbia County Courthouse – 173 NE Hernando Avenue, Lake City.\nB. Lake City Annex (Court Administration) – 4424 NW American Lane, Lake City.\nC. Dixie County Courthouse – 214 NE Hwy 351, Cross City.\nD. Hamilton County Courthouse – 207 NE 1st Street, Jasper.\nE. Lafayette County Courthouse – 120 W Main Street, Mayo.\nF. Madison County Courthouse – 125 SW Range Avenue, Madison.\nG. Madison County Courthouse Annex – 229 SW Pinckney St, Madison.\nH. Suwannee County Courthouse – 200 S Ohio Avenue, Live Oak.\nI. Suwannee County Judicial Annex – 218 Parshley St SW, Live Oak.\nJ. Taylor County Courthouse – 108 N Jefferson Street, Peny.\nK. Facilities ancillary to the courthouses accessed by the public for the purpose of\nconducting the necessary business of the courts as required by the constitution,\nstatutes, or court rules; and,\nL. Any other facilities subsequently designated for court or court related functions to\ninclude temporary designations if necessary.\n1 This order does not affect the rights enumerated in Florida Statote 790.251 under the “Preservation and Protection\nof the Right to Keep and Bear Arms in Motor Vehicles Act of 2008 ,”\n2\nAO 2025-005 (Court Facility Security Procedures Within the Third Judicial Circuit)\nII. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF SHERIFFS\nThe safety and security of court facilities have historically been entrusted to the Sheriff of\neach county to operate as they deem appropriate and with consultation and cooperation with the\njudiciary. The Sheriffs of the Third Judicial Circuit shall provide security for the comt facilities\nof the circuit and county courts, their personnel, clerks’ staff ( acting as an arm of the judicial\ncourt in furtherance of court business), jurors, attorneys and the public who access court\nfacilities. For purposes of this Administrative Order, a “bailiff” is defined as a law enforcement\nofficer appointed by the Sheriff and ce1tified under chapter 943 of the Florida Statutes, who is\nassigned by a Sheriff to provide security to court facilities on a full time or part-time basis.\nIII. SECURITY GUIDELINES FOR ENTERING COURT FACILITIES\nExcept as set forth below, all persons entering court facilities through public access\nportals shall be subject to identification verification and search. Searches may be conducted at\nall points of public ingress under procedures established by the She1iffs using personnel and\nequipment approved by them. Searches shall include protocols, techniques, and equipment\nmost likely to detect contraband, weapons, fireanns, flammable, hazardous or toxic materials,\nbombs, biological and chemical agents. Sheriffs are authorized by applicable Florida law to\nconfiscate prohibited objects seized from persons entering the court facility. Items which have\nbeen confiscated but are lawful to possess outside of the court facility may be returned when the\nowner departs the courthouse premises.\nAll visitors in attendance at circuit or county court events in courtrooms, hearing rooms,\nor chambers may be screened by a bailiff prior to entering. Screening shall be sufficient\nto ensure that no firearms, weapons, or destructive devices shall enter the courtroom,\nhearing room, or chambers. Minimum screening requirements shall include a bailiff to\nconduct the screening, use of a metal detector, a barrier to limit free ingress, and a search\nof personal articles of sufficient size to hide a weapon. An x-ray machine may be used in\nlieu of a personal search.\nPersons refusing to be searched shall be denied access to court facilities. Persons found\nto be in possession of contraband or illegal weapons, illegal firearms or hazardous materials shall\nbe, in the discretion of comthouse security officers, arrested or referred for investigation to the\nappropriate law enforcement agency.\nAny person engaged in activities observed by judges or courthouse security to be a threat\nto the safety of persons or property in a court facility, or who disrupts official business in the\ncourts or in its ancillary facilities, or who violates state, county, or municipal laws, shall, in the\ndiscretion of court facility security officers, be subject to arrest and/or ejection from the facility\nupon order of a judge or duly authorized law enforcement officer.\nNo food or drinks will be pennitted within the courthouse. An exception shall be made\nfor attorneys and necessary staff who will be in the comthouse for extended periods of time.\nThey may b1ing in sealed bottles of water or an empty reusable bottle of water.\n3\nAO 2025-005 (Court Facility Security Procedures Within the Third Judicial Circuit)\nIV. PERSONS EXEMPT FROM SEARCH\nWith the consent of the Chief Judge and in coordination with courthouse security and\nelected Clerks of Court, the Trial Court Administrator may issue, control, and revoke Third\nCircuit identification documents regulating secured access to court facilities. The following\npersons shall be exempt from search when entering or departing court facilities:\nA. Judges and magistrates of the Third Circuit, and the Trial Court Administrator;\nB. Persons displaying a current Third Circuit identification document issued or\napproved by the Trial Court Administrator authorized to enter through nonpublic\nor designated employee entrances;\nC. Upon proof of proper identification, federal, state, county, and municipal law\nenforcement officers when on official business;\nD. The elected Third Circuit State Attorney, Public Defender, Sheriffs, and\nClerks of Court.\nV. FIREARMS AND WEAPONS CONTROL\nA. General Prohibition\nExcept as authorized by this Administrative Order or any applicable statutory law, no\nperson is pennitted to carry into court facilities any contraband, weapons, firearms, ammunition,\nnon-lethal personal protection devices, flammable, hazardous or toxic materials, bombs, or\nbiological or chemical agents.\nB. Exemption: Clerks and Evidence Custodians\nThe elected Clerks of Court are permitted to possess a firearm in their personal offices\nbut are not permitted to carry firearms or weapons in other areas of court facilities or in\ncourtrooms, unless otherwise provided herein.\nItems which are intended to be introduced in court as evidence, or which are in the\ncustody of the clerk as evidence, shall be admitted into court facilities provided they are\nmaintained in secure containers and in safe condition and made available for inspection while on\ncourt facility premises and grounds.\nC. Exemption: Judges and Circuit Employees\nJudges are permitted to carry firearms in court facilities. Judicial assistants are authorized\nto carry non-lethal protection devices including, but not limited to, tasers, mace and pepper\nspray. The Trial Court Administrator is permitted to carry firearms in court facilities with\npermission from the Chief Judge.\n4\nAO 2025-005 (Court Facility Security Procedures Within the Third Judicial Circuit)\n5\nD. Exemption: Marshals and Judges from Florida Supreme Court and District\nCourts of Appeal\nWhen in a Third Judicial Circuit court facility on official business, the justices, judges\nand Marshals of the Florida Supreme Court and District Courts of Appeal are permitted to\ncarry firearms in court facilities.\nE. Exemption: Deputy Sheriffs Assigned to Court Facility Security\nDeputy Sheriffs assigned as bailiffs or court facility security are permitted to carry\nfirearms in court facilities as authorized by applicable statute.\nAll bailiffs or court facility security who are authorized to carry firearms as part of their\nofficial duties are prohibited from carrying a firearm into any court facility in this circuit when\nthe law enforcement officer is a party to the proceeding or is not appearing in an official capacity.\nF. Exemption: Certain Law Enforcement Officers2\n1. The following law enforcement officers who meet the requirements listed in this\nsection are also permitted to carry firearms or weapons in court facilities while\nperforming their official duties:\na. County Sheriffs and Deputy Sheriffs of the Third Judicial Circuit;\nb. Law enforcement officers employed by a local police department and holding\nactive certification from the Criminal Justice Standards and Training\nCommission pursuant to F.S. 943.1395, whose agency is headquartered within\nthe Third Judicial Circuit;\nc. Investigators employed by the State Attorney who are authorized by the State\nAttorney to carry firearms; and,\nd. Law enforcement officers from federal law enforcement agencies.\n2. The excepted law enforcement officers listed above may enter or occupy a court\nfacility with a firearm or weapon provided that the officer meets all of the\nfollowing requirements:\na. is in a recognized law enforcement uniform or wearing visible identification\nthat identifies them as law enforcement; and,\nb. provides appropriate identification with a photograph (a badge alone is not\nsufficient);\nc. is in the court facility on official business; and,\nd. has any firearm in his or her possession in a secure holster, and has any\nother weapon similarly secured on the officer.\n3. Each judge retains the discretion to prohibit the exempted law enforcement\n_______________________\n2 Law enforcement officers mean individuals meeting the definition set forth in Florida Statute 943.10(1). It does\nnot include probation officers, process servers or bail bondsmen.\nAO 2025-005 (Court Facility Security Procedures Within the Third Judicial Circuit)\nofficers from carrying weapons in proceedings before him/her. The judge or\npresiding officer may exercise such a prohibition overall or on a case-by-case\nbasis.\n4. All exempted law enforcement officers who are authorized to carry firearms as\npart of their official duties are prohibited from carrying a firearm into any court\nfacility in this circuit when the law enforcement officer is a party to the\nproceeding or is not appearing in an official capacity.\n5. In limited instances where heightened security may be required, upon advance\nnotice to the Chief Judge or Trial Court Administrator and with the consent of the\nassigned judge, Sheriffs may request a waiver of the requirement of wearing a\nuniform or visible identification in order to permit undercover officers to possess\nfirearms or weapons in court facilities.\nG. Exemption: Third Judicial Circuit State Attorney and Assistant State Attorneys\nThe Third Judicial Circuit State Attorney and assistant state attorneys who are authorized\nby the elected State Attorney to carry firearms as part of their official duties are permitted to\ncarry firearms into and out of court facilities where their offices are located in the same court\nfacility. Under no circumstances are they permitted to carry firearms into a judge’s chambers,\ncourt administration offices, courtrooms or hearing rooms housed in the same building as their\noffice.\nThe State Attorney and all assistant state attorneys who are authorized by the elected\nState Attorney to carry firearms as part of their official duties are prohibited from carrying a\nfirearm into any court facility in this circuit when they are not representing the interests of the\nState of Florida or appearing in an official capacity. Additionally, if the State Attorney or an\nassistant state attorney is present in a court facility for a personal matter, s/he is expressly\nprohibited from carrying a firearm into the court facility.\nH. Exceptional or Emergency Circumstances\nAt their discretion, any Third Judicial Circuit Sheriff may temporarily prohibit any\npersons authorized by this administrative order from carrying weapons into a court facility. The\nSheriffs may also temporarily authorize representatives oflaw enforcement agencies to carry\nweapons into a court facility when needed for assistance with the Sheriff’s response to an\nexceptional, emergency or exigent circumstance.\nVI. COURTROOM ASSIGNMENTS, OFFICE HOURS, INGRESS AND EGRESS\nIn consultation with court facility security and the Clerks, the Chief Judge shall regulate\nthe use of courtrooms, establish the dockets, determine the hours for the public’s use of the court\nfacilities and the office hours for occupants of court facilities, designate which entrances and\nexits shall be public and private and accessible by court staff or the public, establish rules for\nafter-hours access by authorized personnel, location of bailiff stations, and procedures for\ncontrolled access to secure and non-secure areas. The Chief Judge may designate areas of court\n6\nAO 2025-005 (Court Facility Security Procedures Within the Third Judicial Circuit)\nfacilities that are to be secured and accessible only by authorized personnel. Access to secure\nareas shall be monitored by court security to prevent intrusion.\nVII. PUBLIC DEMONSTRATIONS AND PROTECTIONS OF JURORS AND COURT\nPERSONNEL\nIt is crucial to the administration of justice that movement of persons into and out of court\nfacilities be unimpeded, and that judges, attorneys, litigants, and jurors be allowed to perform\ntheir duty on the premises without undue interference and without being improperly approached\nor influenced.\nCourt facility security officers shall prohibit any activity which is perceived to be a threat\nto the safety of persons or property within court facilities or on court facilities grounds, or which\ndisrupts the official business conducted within such facilities, or which may reasonably be\nconstrued as an attempt to influence or intimidate jurors, litigants or judges, or which constitutes\na violation of Florida Statute, county ordinance, or administrative order of this Court.\nORDERED this 1st day of October, in Chambers, Lake City, Columbia County, Florida,\nand effective immediately.\n\nSigned:  Melissa G. Please do not call the Court expecting to speak with a judge about any case. The Court is only allowed to consider evidence and arguments made in the courtroom and in documents properly filed by actual parties in the case as authorized by law and the Rules of Court. The Court cannot ethically read or consider any other evidence or arguments about the case.  Ex parte communications also applies to the General Magistrate & Hearing Officers.\n\nF.S. 668.6076\n\nUnder Florida law, e-mail addresses are public records. Help\nFacebook-f\n \nX-twitter\nIMPORTANT COURT AND WEATHER ALERTS\nAO 2022-05\nDownload the PDF\nIN THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT OF FLORIDA\nADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO.\n2022-05\nIN RE:ORDER OF COURT DECORUM FOR THE THIRD JUDICIAL CIRCUIT\n\nWHEREAS, the Court is charged with the responsibility of maintaining proper order and decorum. Accordingly, the Court shall require all spectators, witnesses, observers, litigants, jurors, and others with whom the judge deals in an official capacity, to conduct and dress themselves in a manner deemed fitting and respectable.\n\nIt is therefore ORDERED as follows:\n\n1. Dress in the courtroom and chambers:\n\nNo tank tops, cropped shirts, spaghetti strapped shirts or the like. No bare midriffs or shoulders.\nNo clothing with inappropriate printing thereon. No pajamas.\nNo shorts except for children under 12 years of age. No bare feet.\nNo flip-flops.\nNo hats, caps worn.\nNo sunglasses worn unless required for a medical condition.\nNo head coverings except for recognized religious beliefs/practices. (You will be required to show your face to security prior to entry.)\nNo head or face coverings. (Subject to covid-19 masks exceptions.)\n\n2. Decorum and Behavior in the Courtroom and Chambers:\n\nWhile in session, everyone is required to remain silent except for those presently involved with the case before the court or you’re speaking with your attorney.\nNo eating or drinking. No gum chewing.\nAll cellular phones or audible electronic devices shall be silenced.\nNo racist, sexist, obscene, or profane language.\nNo person shall bring packages, suitcases, boxes, duffel bags, shopping bags or containers into the courtroom without prior approval of the bailiff.\n\n3. Enforcement of said decorum policy will be by the bailiffs of this circuit.\n\n4. Failure to abide by these court rules and regulations may result in a contempt finding and the assessment of a fine.\n\nThis decorum policy shall be construed as the minimum decorum standards that shall be adhered to throughout the Third Judicial Circuit. Each presiding judge may implement more stringent guidelines as deemed appropriate.\n\nDONE AND ORDERED in Columbia County, Florida, on October 26 , 2022.\n\nMark E. Feagle, Chief Judge\n\nCopies to:\n\n \n\nMark E. Feagle, Chief Judge\nThird Circuit Clerks\nState Attorney\nPublic Defender\nAll Judges of the TJC\nBack To Orders\n\n\n\n\n\nPress Escape to close the search panel.\nX Feed | Circuit3FL\n\nJudge Kathryn R.
